comments.author: @Aodès-v5k
comments.text: Je travaille très fort contre cette éventualité. J'aime le Canada et je ne laisserai pas la séparation se faire sans mon combat à mon niveau. Les vieilles querelles doivent se résorber. Ce qui est acceptable doit être accepté. Il ne s'agit pas de nier l'histoire, mais de construire ce qu'il faut pour qu'elle s'améliore. Construire des ponts entre les cultures, les idées. Réconcilier les cousins. Les descendants des Anglais qui ont brimés mes ancêtres sont différents de leurs ancêtres et je ne saurais pas les rendre responsable de ma situation personnelle. Le Commonwealth est une bonne chose pour l'humanité. La royauté anglaise a beaucoup évolué depuis le dernier siècle et ne représente dorénavant plus ce racisme absurde d'autrefois. I would kneel to the King for its symbol as it has become. Hear me well : I was separatist until 1997 but I realized. Now I'm proud to be a proud canadian AND proud at the face of my french canadian ancesters. Love will prevail !

comments.author: @pl.simard
comments.text: What every video about Quebec independance says that it's the third time we're trying to be a country. What they all forget to mention is that Quebec was french colonies assimilated by British ones. We WERE our own country, it just got stolen from us because France decided to not defend us. US colonies didn't either. They separated from Britain but didn't want to help us separate from France. Also, for the 1995 referendum, federal gouvernment manipulated first nations votes and managed to raise the level of immigration in Quebec province. All new immigrants obviously wouldn't want to separate from Canada, the country who welcomed them, and federal gouvernment knew it. They also made a fear campaign to scare our population on what would happen if we were to leave ... We would already be a country if the rest of Canada wouldn't have manipulated our voters. (sorry for my not native english ...)

comments.author: @mike62mcmanus
comments.text:
They fined old-age homes for having English on the bulletin board. How mean is that? Quebec's Bill 101 to protect the French language, was challenged as unfair and went to the Supreme Court.
It took ten years for a decision, and the decision was that: Yes, it was unfair, but it had been in place so long that to change it now would be unfair... Never trust the courts, especially the ones in ermine coats.
